type.description:
One of the supported threshold types:
- `absolute-low`:
   The threshold defines an absolute minimum "triggering value". If the
   signal's value becomes equal or lower, the threshold enters a "triggered"
   state. If the value grows back up and exceeds the "re-arming value",
   the threshold leaves its "triggered" state, and only then is eligible
   for triggering again.
- `absolute-high`:
   The threshold defines an absolute maximum "triggering value". If the
   signal's value becomes equal or higher, the threshold enters a "triggered"
   state. If the value falls back down and exceeds the "re-arming value",
   the threshold leaves its "triggered" state, and only then is eligible
   for triggering again.

A set of thresholds configured for a specific model's signal must be
consistent, i.e. it must define disjoint regions of active thresholds.
In other words: it may not allow any situation in which two different
thresholds are in their "triggered" state.

Please note that a threshold of the same type, configured for a more
extreme severity (and thus, a higher severity) overrides the region of the
less extreme threshold.

An example valid configuration containing both types of thresholds:

| type          | value | rearm | severity |
| ------------- | ----- | ----- | -------- |
| absolute-high | 39    | 31    | 80       |
| absolute-high | 31    | 27    | 20       |
| absolute-low  | 17    | 18    | 30       |
| absolute-low  | 15    | 15    | 80       |
| absolute-low  | 10    | 11    | 90       |

The following fields are available for both filtering and sorting: - `id`: ID of the transfer - `machine.id`: ID of the machine - `machine.name`: name of the machine - `model.id`: ID of the model - `model.name`: name of the model - `fileName`: name of the transferred file - `fileExtension`: extension of the transferred file - `sizeInBytes`: size in bytes of the transferred file - `createdAt`: transfer creation time - `complete`: transfer completion status (`true` or `false`)
